stem_book: Each copper (II) sulphate unit is associated with water molecules. When this compound is heated in air above 100°C, it loses the water molecules and also its colour: CuSO₄·xH₂O → CuSO₄ + xH₂O. If 9.60 g of CuSO₄ are left after heating 15.01 g of the blue compound, calculate the number of moles of H₂O originally present per mole of CuSO₄ in the compound (i.e. x). (Cu = 63.5, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1)
